value.rationale: Near-boundary Dirichlet evaluation provides a mathematically intrinsic critical family, with exactly the minimal inverse moment for trace class. Trace-norm convergence of the *entire* nonzero spectrum for arbitrary measure types and a uniform explicit error is a structural universality law, not a finite-parameter table or mere trace asymptotic. The surprising strong-operator collapse simultaneous with nonzero norm and exact first Euler trace correction explain how spectral mass escapes to high Dirichlet coefficients. A smooth gamma special case was already known; this qualitative universality is not implied by it.
